//: Differences from the pre-refactor baseline that are intended.
snapshot:verify compares against a capture taken before the module framework
existed. Anything not listed here is a regression. Anything listed here is a
decision someone made on purpose, with the reason next to it — which is the
whole point: the list of everything this refactor deliberately changed is one
reviewable file rather than a memory of which failures were 'fine'.
`path` is a JSON path into the captured file; everything under it is
accepted too, so '$.body.modules' covers the whole subtree. Use bracket
notation for a key containing dots: "$['report.csv']".
`field` instead of `path` strips that key at any depth, for a field added to
every row of a list. `file` may end in `*` for path and field entries alike.

accepted.why: New key. Configured module instances. Empty on an installation whose settings.json predates modules — the registry derives the ActivoBank and Pricempire instances from the old `schedules` and `internal.profile` keys instead, so nothing that already existed changed value.

New endpoints, one group per configured instance: what the interface reads to know which modules exist and what each offers, each instance's configuration, and each one's status. The per-provider routes they generalise (/google/status, /pricempire/status, /ingest/activobank, …) all still exist and still answer exactly the same thing — the entries for those are compared as before, and are unchanged.

Not a captured file — recorded here so the one visible change in the interface is written down somewhere. The Settings schedules table now names each module from its manifest's translation key, so it reads 'Leitura do email ActivoBank' in Portuguese instead of the hardcoded English 'ActivoBank email scan'. The old list was a literal object of five English strings, which broke the rule that no user-visible text is a literal, and would have shown a fork's own bank as a bare id. Everything else on Connections, Rules and Settings is pixel-identical.

Gone from the capture, and they were noise. Documents are now re-read by the module instance that stored them; Pricempire declares no bank-document parser, so its portfolio exports are skipped. The baseline entries were those CSVs fed to the ActivoBank statement parsers, which read zero transactions out of a hundred rows each and reported one unparsed line — a measurement of nothing.

New endpoint. GET /api/analytics/flow, the income → account → category aggregate behind the Money flow card. Deliberately its own route rather than two more fields on /analytics: that response is in this baseline, and keeping it byte-identical is what makes this whole comparison a signal. Nothing asks for this endpoint unless a dashboard node is drawing it.
New endpoint. GET /api/analytics/daily, one row per day with spending, behind the Spending calendar card. Same reasoning as the flow route above.

New endpoint. GET /api/currency/rates, the whole exchange-rate table now that the app converts between forty-five currencies rather than two. The single-pair routes it generalises (/currency/rate and its refresh) are deliberately untouched and are compared as before — if either of those ever drifts, that is a bug in the wrapper, not a diff to accept.

Gone. It briefly held a flag per experimental chart. Those charts are now ordinary entries in the dashboard's widget catalogue, added and removed by the reader, so the flag was a second place to switch on something the add/remove gesture already governs.

New key. The cards the dashboard is made of, in the order they are drawn: {id, widget, view, size} per node. `view` lives on the node rather than in the browser, which is both how a view preference survives a restart and how the same widget can appear twice on one dashboard as a chart and as a table. The shipped default is six cards; this installation's own settings.json carries twelve, which is a data fact rather than a default.

New keys `rates` and `manual` beside the old `usdToEur`, which is still written and still holds the same number. Conversion used to be one dollar-to-euro scalar; it is now a table against the euro pivot, because the app ships fourteen languages and 'the dollar rate' is not a currency system. `loadSettings` migrates the scalar into `rates.USD` on read, so an installation that predates the table sees no change in what anything is worth.

Shape change: each entry is now {key, params} instead of a finished sentence. It was the last hardcoded Portuguese string the server put on screen — 'X% do que gastaste foi em Y' — which read Portuguese in all fourteen languages. Nothing in the interface renders this field today, so the visible effect is nil; the point is that it can now be rendered in the reader's language when something does.

Deliberate, personal-data fix. Eduardo had hand-made an "in-account moviment" category (state/categories.json, not a shipped default) for term-deposit constitute/reinforce/liquidate rows (CONSTIT/REFORCO/LIQ DEP PRAZO) — self-moves the account-pairing heuristic never recognises, because none of that wording matches a transfer pattern. Nothing ever excluded it from spending, so €8,453 across 34 transactions counted as real income and expense on every dashboard chart. The `excludeFromSpending` flag existed on the shipped `internal_transfer` category already; this session wired it up (see the next entry) and then set it on Eduardo's own category too, in `user-data/`, matching CLAUDE.md's rule that a personal-data problem is fixed in the data, not in the defaults.

2822 → 2788, and the same 34-row drop flows into `monthlyCashflow`, `categoryBreakdown`, `categoryTrend` and `cumulative` for June–August 2026. `spendingTransactions` (server/projections/rebuild.js) now excludes any transaction whose category is flagged `excludeFromSpending` in the category registry, not only one whose `internal` boolean was set by the account-pairing heuristic. This tool reports only the first differing path per file, alphabetically, so `allocation` (an unrelated, pre-existing market-data drift, already accepted above) is what actually prints; this entry exists so the real, deeper diff those 34 rows cause is not mistaken for something this tool silently missed. Confirmed directly against a freshly booted server: `range.matched` was 2822 before this session's `in-account moviment` flag and 2788 after.

//: Below this line: not caused by any code change. The baseline was captured
on 2026-08-11 and the ledger has lived since — quotes refreshed, a sync ran,
an appearance switch was flipped. They are listed rather than silently
tolerated so that the next person can tell a stale baseline from a
regression, which is the one distinction this file exists to preserve.
Re-taking the baseline would clear them and hide whatever drifted alongside.
accepted.why: api/assets.json, api/investments*.json, api/securities.json and api/analytics*.json allocation values move with the market — the CS2 position is 475.35 → 461.05 as of this writing, because the quote fetcher keeps running. api/events.json $.body.bytes grew with the ledger, which is 2912 movements in the baseline and 2989 now: statements have been ingested since, so api/transactions.json, api/accounts*.json, documents.json and everything derived from them differ by exactly that. api/settings.json $.body.appearance.locale went pt → en and $.body.appearance.textures false → true because the switches were flipped in Settings. Thirty-four of fifty-eight files differ on this count alone, and the same thirty-four differ with the dashboard work reverted — which is how it was checked. Re-taking the baseline would clear them and hide whatever drifted alongside.

The tail bucket is now the sentinel 'other' rather than the literal 'Outros'. The dashboard folded a second time into its own translated "Other", so the legend carried two fold buckets and one of them was Portuguese whatever language the interface was set to. The engine emits a key and the card names it.

Trips now read as `travel` while settings.analytics.travelOverlay is on (the default). Claiming a transaction for a trip no longer overwrites its category, so the fold that used to be written into the ledger is applied at read time instead — the same figures, arrived at without destroying what the transaction actually was. Turning the setting off restores the un-folded breakdown.
Same overlay as categoryBreakdown above.
Same overlay as categoryBreakdown above: insights are computed from the breakdown.

Anomaly findings no longer carry a `travel` field or the during-a-trip wording. A transaction inside a trip is now skipped outright, so the branch that produced them cannot be reached: the exemption used to require inside-a-trip AND categorized `travel`, which only made sense while claiming a transaction for a trip overwrote its category.

Trips are a tag and no longer a category. Marking a transaction for a trip writes only the tag event, `POST /travels/:id/apply` no longer categorizes at all, and `travelAnomalies` reads the tag rather than `tx.category === 'travel'` — so the missing/stray counts move. The movements themselves keep the categories they already had.

New endpoint. GET /api/networth, accounts plus holdings by class. Its own route rather than a field on /accounts, which is in this baseline and is a different question anyway — half of what this returns is not in a bank.

New endpoint. GET /travels/spending, what each trip cost broken down by real category. The one endpoint that deliberately ignores the travel overlay: a card reporting that a trip cost EUR 2,000 and that 100% of it was travel would be the information loss the refactor exists to undo.
New key. `travelOverlay`, on by default: whether the dashboard reads trip spending as one travel category. A reading choice, nothing on disk.
New key. Which classes of holding count toward net worth, per class. Absent means counted.

Investing is its own flow (server/engines/investing.js): a movement into an ETF, a broker, an exchange or a skin marketplace is neither income nor spending. New per-row field: the reason a movement counts as investing (link, order, category, counterparty), absent when it does not.

Investing is its own flow (server/engines/investing.js): a movement into an ETF, a broker, an exchange or a skin marketplace is neither income nor spending. New per-row field on rows a marketplace module wrote for its own trades (Pricempire's "Buy 1x …"). They describe a holding, not money leaving an account, and leave every flow total; the bank debit is the money.

Travel is no longer a category (server/lib/derivedCategories.js): category assignments that said `travel` are skipped in the fold, so those movements keep the category they had before, or return to the review queue when travel was all they ever had. New per-row field marking the movements that once carried it, so the Travel page can hand them to a trip.

Investing is its own flow (server/engines/investing.js): a movement into an ETF, a broker, an exchange or a skin marketplace is neither income nor spending. Every aggregate moves with it: the cashflow gains an `invested` column and its expense drops by what was invested; breakdowns, trend, merchants, calendar, shifts, amortized view and insights are drawn from consumption only; the flow sends investing to its own nodes. Marketplace position rows leave the totals. Travel is no longer a category (server/lib/derivedCategories.js): category assignments that said `travel` are skipped in the fold, so those movements keep the category they had before, or return to the review queue when travel was all they ever had. The analytics response also gains `previous` (the prior span's totals for the headline tiles), the prior span is calendar-aligned (September against August, not the 30 days before), and granularity=week is now weekly instead of silently monthly.
New endpoint. GET /api/analytics/pace, a month's cumulative spending by day against the month before and a typical month, behind the Spending pace card.
New endpoint. GET /api/travels/:id/summary, one trip per day and per category, behind the single-trip card.

Investing is its own flow (server/engines/investing.js): a movement into an ETF, a broker, an exchange or a skin marketplace is neither income nor spending. New key: `counterparties`, null meaning the shipped list.

Each trip's `transactionCount` and `total` are now what the trip *claimed* rather than everything between its dates (which counted the rent and the salary of that week), and it gains `reviewWindow` and `toReview`: the late tail, seven days after the trip, where charges that post after coming home are offered for review.
The trip screen lists the late tail too (up to seven days after the trip, debits only), sorted by date, each late row saying it is after the trip and, when it looks like part of it, why.
New list: charges after a trip that look like they came from it (paid abroad, or at a merchant already paid during the trip).

Travel is no longer a category (server/lib/derivedCategories.js): category assignments that said `travel` are skipped in the fold, so those movements keep the category they had before, or return to the review queue when travel was all they ever had. New list: movements once filed as travel that no trip claims, each with the trip it most likely belonged to.

Travel is no longer a category (server/lib/derivedCategories.js): category assignments that said `travel` are skipped in the fold, so those movements keep the category they had before, or return to the review queue when travel was all they ever had. This is the change the user asked for: a trip claimed under the old model read as 100% travel, and now reads as what it was spent on.
New default category `accommodation` (hotels, Airbnb), which is where the old travel keywords for lodging point; `travel` is now system and derived; `investments` carries `investment: true`.

Not a captured file. The rows that change category because of the travel fold above — in transactions*.json, transactions_pending*.json, suggestions_*.json and projections.json — cannot be named by path; they are exactly the movements carrying `legacyTravel`, and nothing else should differ there. Suggestions also stop offering `travel` (the lodging keywords now say `accommodation`, the airline ones `transport`), and the CS2 marketplaces suggest `investments` instead of `gaming`.
New endpoint. GET /api/recurring, bills and income inferred from the ledger (server/engines/recurring.js), behind the Upcoming bills card and the forecast.
New endpoint. GET /api/analytics/forecast, today's cash from the printed balances, the last thirty days and the weeks ahead (server/engines/forecast.js).
New endpoint. GET /api/analytics/runway, the typical month over the last twelve complete ones, behind the Runway & independence card.
New endpoint. GET /api/budgets, this month against the per-category goals (server/engines/budgets.js), and each category's usual month as a suggested goal.
New key: the withdrawal rate and real return the independence projection assumes.
New key: the filter-bar states the reader saved as named views.
